title: How many dimensions does it really have?
sub: A curve in the plane, measured two ways.

frames.caption: 600 points on a spiral: a one-dimensional curve living in two dimensions. Walk along it and you only ever have one direction to go.

PCA looks for flat directions of spread. The spiral's points spread almost equally in both: 61% and 39% of the variance. PCA would call this data 2-dimensional. Curvature fools any linear method: a curved 1-D manifold needs several flat directions to contain it, so PCA overestimates.

The Two-NN estimator looks only at each point's two nearest neighbours. On a k-dimensional manifold the ratio μ = r₂/r₁ of their distances follows a law that depends only on k: plotting −log(1 − F(μ)) against log μ gives a straight line of slope k. For the spiral (blue) the slope is 1.07.

For comparison, points filling a disk (orange), which really is two-dimensional, give slope 2.04. Because it only uses distances to the closest neighbours, where any smooth manifold looks flat, Two-NN measures the intrinsic dimension (1 for the spiral) rather than the ambient one, curved or not.
